I don't know the default `separator_regex` of `TokenTextSplitter` from the provided documents. They don't state it.

The closest relevant material is the usage example, which shows the parameters `chunk_size`, `chunk_overlap`, and `separator`:

"splitter = TokenTextSplitter(chunk_size=1024, chunk_overlap=20, separator=" ")" [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/loading/node_parsers/modules.md]

That example sets `separator=" "` explicitly, but it doesn't show a `separator_regex` parameter or its default. In fact, as far as these documents show, `TokenTextSplitter` takes a `separator`, not a `separator_regex`. A regex-based separator parameter is something I'd associate with other splitters, but the context doesn't confirm that either. The API reference page [llama_index/docs/api_reference/api_reference/node_parsers/token_text_splitter.md] only points to the class and doesn't list its defaults.

To confirm, check the source file linked from the contributing guide: `llama-index-core/llama_index/core/node_parser/text/token.py`.
